canonFrame.editionAssumptions: Use Cyberpunk RED and Night City 2045 as the default tabletop layer. Treat Cyberpunk 2020 as history and Cyberpunk 2077 as a later, separate era. Do not back-port 2077 districts, corporate control, technologies, characters, or political outcomes into 2045 without an explicit campaign choice.
canonFrame.timelineNotes: Night City was transformed by the Fourth Corporate War and the 2023 nuclear destruction of the city center. By 2045 it is rebuilding through a patchwork of municipal government, corporations, neighborhoods, gangs, nomads, and local services. By 2077 it has changed again. Preserve those decades as distinct settings rather than a single neon present.

campaignFoundations: Night City is a specific independent city within the Free State of Northern California, not the whole Cyberpunk world.
The default era is 2045, during reconstruction after the Fourth Corporate War and the nuclear disaster of 2023.
Corporate power is immense, but the city is not governed by one corporation.
Street reputation, contacts, favors, logistics, and access matter as much as cash.
Cyberware is common enough to shape society but remains medical, economic, psychological, and legal reality.
Violence is frequent, yet neighborhoods, communities, media, commerce, art, and ordinary work continue.
The old global Net is dangerous and fragmented; local architectures and the Data Pool define much of 2045 network life.
Gangs, security companies, fixers, nomads, corporations, and government agencies overlap without controlling every block.
Style, identity, and public image are survival tools.
The player characters should build their own legend rather than orbit canonical video-game protagonists.
gameMasterGuidance: Ask whether the campaign uses 2045 or 2077 before naming district conditions or corporate dominance.
Create jobs through concrete clients, constraints, collateral risks, and incomplete information.
Track reputation and relationships separately from money.
Make cyberware installation, maintenance, therapy, legality, and supply part of the world.
Use neighborhoods as communities, not disposable combat maps.
Let media narratives alter consequences after a job.
Distinguish gangs, organized crime, security contractors, police, and corporations.
Preserve scarcity and damaged infrastructure in 2045.
Mark invented bars, gangs, fixers, businesses, and blocks as campaign-created.
canonBoundaries: Do not blend the 2020, 2045, and 2077 eras.
Do not assume the outcomes or protagonists of Cyberpunk 2077 are present in 2045.
Night City is not a sovereign country, though it has unusual local autonomy and free-port status.
Do not treat every corporate employee as a combat operative or every gang member as irrational.
Do not make the 2045 Net identical to 2077 quickhacking.
Do not make all cyberpsychosis automatic, immediate, or morally simple.
Do not portray nomads as generic desert raiders.
Do not turn every district into uninterrupted neon luxury; reconstruction, rubble, temporary systems, and local variation matter.
Do not use rules prices as proof that an item is available.
Avoid forcing famous bars, fixers, solos, or corporations into every job.

referenceChunks.title: History of Night City
referenceChunks.text: Night City began as Richard Night's privately planned city on the central California coast. It was originally called Coronado City and was intended to be a modern corporate and commercial hub. Night's murder turned the project into a struggle among his successors, organized crime, corporations, local government, and outside powers. The city took his name and developed a reputation for opportunity, violence, rapid construction, and weak public control. Through the early twenty-first century, Night City became a center of corporate competition, media, technology, organized crime, and mercenary work. The Fourth Corporate War escalated conflict between major corporations, especially Arasaka and Militech, into global warfare. In 2023 a nuclear device detonated in the city's corporate center during an assault on Arasaka Tower. The blast and its aftermath destroyed or contaminated central districts, killed large numbers of people, and broke existing systems of government and commerce. The following decades are called the Time of the Red, named for skies stained by particulate pollution and global disaster. Shipping, manufacturing, communications, and national power fragmented. Night City survived through reconstruction, local production, salvage, nomad transport, corporate return, and neighborhood adaptation. By 2045, the city is neither a post-apocalyptic ruin nor the polished 2077 metropolis. New development stands beside hot zones, temporary settlements, repaired infrastructure, and districts under uneven authority. The destruction of 2023 is living memory for older residents and a source of myth for younger edgerunners. Use history to explain current grudges, land claims, missing records, contaminated sites, corporate propaganda, and families displaced more than once.

referenceChunks.title: Legal Status and Government
referenceChunks.text: In 2045 Night City is part of the Free State of Northern California. It is an independent city in the legal sense that it is not subordinate to a surrounding county, and it operates as a free port with comparatively loose restrictions on corporate and commercial activity. It is not a separate sovereign nation. Municipal government includes a city council, city managers, administrative offices, and public-service contracts. Formal government competes with corporations, security providers, neighborhood organizations, gangs, property owners, criminal groups, and emergency arrangements. A law can be real without being enforced in every district. A city office can exist while lacking staff, data, vehicles, or authority on the street. Citizenship and official identity matter for services, voting, property, employment, and legal standing. People without reliable records may survive through community recognition, forged documents, corporate identity, nomad family affiliation, or cash. The disaster and migration of previous decades produced many broken or disputed identities. Municipal politics revolve around reconstruction, development contracts, security, utilities, zoning, transport, corporate influence, and which communities receive investment. Corruption need not mean a council member takes a bag of cash; it can involve favorable maps, delayed inspections, selective policing, privatized infrastructure, or data that quietly disappears. In play, identify which authority claims a location and which one can actually act there. A corporation may own a building, a security provider patrol the street, a gang control the residents, and the city tax the property. Conflicting legitimate claims are a natural source of jobs and consequences.

referenceChunks.title: Geography and Districts
referenceChunks.text: Night City 2045 is divided into twenty-four districts spread across the Island, Northside, Mainland, and Southside. Each district has its own population, management, security arrangement, recent history, and mixture of formal and informal control. District boundaries matter for policing, utilities, transport, property values, and reputation. The rebuilt city contains luxury development, corporate enclaves, dense housing, commercial strips, ports, industrial areas, suburban remnants, combat zones, reclaimed blocks, and sites still affected by the 2023 destruction. The old city center and Hot Zone remain especially dangerous because of contamination, unstable structures, scavenging, buried infrastructure, and conflicting claims. District names and conditions differ between 2045 and 2077. A familiar 2077 location may not yet exist, may have another function, or may be controlled by a different group. Use the 2045 map for the default era rather than relying on video-game geography. Travel time depends on bridges, transit, road condition, checkpoints, gang territory, traffic, and current violence. Two neighborhoods close on a map can be socially distant. People often identify strongly with a district, megabuilding, block, housing collective, or market. When inventing a location, anchor it to a district's economy and recent history. Decide who provides security, electricity, water, medical care, and dispute resolution. A bar in a corporate district, a market beside a reconstruction zone, and a clinic in gang territory should create different assumptions before a gun is drawn.

referenceChunks.title: Reconstruction and Scarcity
referenceChunks.text: The Time of the Red is defined by disrupted global supply, damaged cities, fragmented institutions, and local rebuilding. Night City has resources and trade, but it does not possess the smooth consumer abundance associated with 2077. Many goods move through salvage, repair, small manufacturing, nomad convoys, regional trade, corporate channels, and informal markets. Availability matters. A character may have enough eurobucks for an item but still need a fixer, market night, corporate contact, or successful favor to locate it. Everyday goods are easier than specialized weapons, cyberware, pharmaceuticals, vehicles, or rare electronics. A shipment delay can change the balance between gangs, clinics, and neighborhoods. Reconstruction is political. Developers want land, city offices want taxable districts, residents want services, corporations want secure facilities, and people living in ruins may be treated as obstacles. Old ownership records were destroyed, manipulated, or rendered meaningless by years of abandonment. Salvage teams enter unstable or contaminated zones for machinery, data, building materials, personal records, and corporate secrets. Recovery can be legal, licensed, stolen, or impossible to classify. Something valuable may also be evidence of who caused a disaster. Use scarcity to generate choices rather than constant deprivation. The crew can secure medicine, reroute a power system, protect a convoy, expose a fraudulent redevelopment, or decide who receives limited equipment. Night City is alive because people improvise systems, not because every vending machine works.

referenceChunks.title: Corporations and the Urban Economy
referenceChunks.text: Corporations remain major powers in 2045, but the Fourth Corporate War damaged many global systems and made corporate return uneven. Companies control secure facilities, research, manufacturing, media, food, medical services, weapons, logistics, and employment. They influence city government through contracts, lobbying, property, intelligence, and private security. Arasaka suffered legal exclusion and political consequences in North America after the war. It should not exercise the same open Night City dominance it holds in 2077. Militech retains strong connections to the New United States and military industry, but it does not simply own the city. Other corporations, subsidiaries, local firms, cooperatives, and informal businesses fill gaps. Corporate employees range from executives and security specialists to technicians, clerks, cleaners, drivers, researchers, and families. A corporate identity can provide housing, healthcare, education, and protection while making survival dependent on obedience. Extraction jobs often concern a person whose skills, contract, data, and dependents cannot be separated. The urban economy includes street vendors, fixers, clinics, artists, repair shops, nomad trade, criminal fronts, cooperatives, and municipal services. Cash matters, but contracts, reputation, access, and debt often matter more. Avoid making corporations omniscient. Departments compete, managers hide failures, databases do not integrate perfectly, and security has budgets. A corporation is most believable when the crew can identify who benefits from a job, who is blamed if it fails, and which internal rival might prefer a different outcome.

referenceChunks.title: Gangs and Organized Crime
referenceChunks.text: Night City contains dozens of gangs and several major criminal organizations. They differ in size, culture, territory, income, political ties, and tolerance for civilians. Some are violent predatory groups. Others combine neighborhood defense, identity, business, mutual aid, and crime. Organized crime maintains deeper financial networks, fronts, corruption, and long-term strategy than many street gangs. Territory is not only painted walls. It can mean control of a market, club circuit, smuggling route, housing block, construction contract, clinic, data source, or protection relationship. A gang may tolerate outsiders who spend money and respect rules while attacking a rival wearing the wrong colors. The 2045 source material includes forty-four gangs, six criminal organizations, and numerous security providers. Do not attempt to insert all of them into one neighborhood. Select groups whose goals intersect with the district and job. Leadership and membership change. A gang's public reputation may lag behind a new boss or splinter. Corporate and government actors sometimes use gangs as proxies, then condemn them publicly. Criminal organizations can negotiate with city officials and corporations without becoming legitimate. In play, give every faction a revenue source, social base, enemy, and limit. Violence should have business and neighborhood consequences. Killing a gang lieutenant may interrupt a drug trade, but it may also end the only patrol protecting residents from a worse group. Do not excuse abuse through community ties; make those contradictions part of the setting.

referenceChunks.title: Law, Security, and Justice
referenceChunks.text: Law enforcement in 2045 is fragmented. The Night City Police Department exists, but staffing, jurisdiction, response, equipment, and political support vary. Private security companies, corporate forces, building security, neighborhood groups, gangs, and deputized providers may perform functions that resemble policing. A call for emergency help does not guarantee a neutral public response. Dispatch considers location, contract, danger, available units, and influence. Corporate enclaves may receive rapid armed response while poorer districts rely on local arrangements. Security providers have reputations and business interests. Justice involves arrest, evidence, plea, fines, confinement, restitution, corporate arbitration, informal settlement, and violence. The legal system is not absent, but unequal access and privatization shape outcomes. Identity records, citizenship, insurance, and employer status affect whether someone is treated as a victim, suspect, employee, or disposable intruder. Edgerunners commonly operate in legal gray zones or commit serious crimes. Their survival depends on concealment, deniability, corrupt contacts, careful target selection, and clients willing to absorb consequences. Police should not appear only after a scripted timer; investigators can follow data, witnesses, weapons, vehicles, medical records, and media. Decide who has jurisdiction before a mission. A building may be protected by corporate contract, the street by a city provider, and the victim by an organized-crime agreement. Conflicting systems create opportunities for forged warrants, negotiated surrender, evidence theft, and blame shifting.

referenceChunks.title: Edgerunners, Fixers, and Street Reputation
referenceChunks.text: Edgerunners are professionals who operate at the margins of law, corporate employment, and conventional security. Crews can include solos, netrunners, techs, medtechs, media, lawmen, executives, rockerboys, nomads, and fixers. These roles describe expertise and social position, not rigid occupations that prevent broader skills. Fixers connect clients, crews, goods, information, and markets. A competent fixer evaluates reliability, conceals identities, negotiates payment, and protects a network. Fixers are not omniscient quest dispensers. They know what their contacts tell them and may pass along a client's lie to preserve business. Street reputation measures what communities believe a person has done and how they behave. It can open doors, deter violence, raise prices, attract rivals, and make anonymity difficult. A legendary job may create the wrong legend if media footage shows collateral damage. Professional norms include meeting security, escrow, partial information, safehouses, burner identities, and consequences for betraying a team. There is no universal edgerunner guild. Trust is personal and local. Build jobs around leverage. Why use deniable outsiders instead of employees or police? What can the client not admit? What makes the target more complicated than the brief? Payment can include cash, gear, treatment, access, records, debt relief, or reputation. The best missions leave the crew with a new relationship and a changed city, not only a body count.

referenceChunks.title: Cyberware, Medicine, and Humanity
referenceChunks.text: Cyberware ranges from replacement limbs and sensory systems to combat implants, neural links, cosmetic modification, and specialized professional tools. It can restore ability, express identity, meet job requirements, create status, or increase violence. Installation requires medical expertise, facilities, compatible components, and recovery. In Cyberpunk RED, extensive augmentation interacts with Humanity and can contribute to cyberpsychosis. This is a game model for alienation, trauma, dissociation, obsession, and loss of empathy in a violent society, not a claim that disabled people, prosthetic users, or anyone with an implant becomes dangerous. Therapy can restore Humanity within rules limits, and social conditions matter. Cyberpsychosis should not function as a surprise punishment for owning one artificial arm. A dangerous breakdown usually emerges through accumulated strain, extreme augmentation, trauma, poor support, and choices. Symptoms can be recognized before indiscriminate violence. Medical and therapeutic characters should have meaningful options. Clinics range from corporate hospitals to neighborhood practices, mobile medtech operations, illegal ripperdocs, and trauma teams. Quality, privacy, price, licensing, and allegiance differ. Medical records can become evidence or corporate property. Cyberware is also a supply chain. Firmware, repair, immunosuppressants, batteries, ammunition, proprietary tools, and replacement parts create dependence. A corporation can control workers through maintenance contracts. A neighborhood clinic can be politically important because it keeps people functional without surrendering their data.

referenceChunks.title: The Net, Local Architectures, and Data Pool
referenceChunks.text: The old global Net was devastated by the Fourth Corporate War, malicious code, rogue artificial intelligences, and the collapse of trusted infrastructure. By 2045, netrunning commonly occurs inside local NET Architectures accessed from physical proximity. Netrunners enter systems that control files, cameras, doors, drones, defenses, and industrial equipment. This makes location matter. A runner cannot generally sit across the world and quickhack every person on a street. The team must reach an access point, protect the netrunner, and coordinate physical and digital objectives. Architecture design reflects an owner's budget and priorities. The Data Pool is a city-scale information environment supporting screamsheets, messages, local services, entertainment, and public data. CitiNet and other infrastructure are more limited and locally managed than the later 2077 Net. Pirate stations, micro-media, and neighborhood channels compete with corporate outlets. Rogue AIs and old Net zones remain dangerous beyond ordinary access. Barriers and organizations attempt to contain them. Do not use later Blackwall assumptions without checking the selected era, though the underlying danger of uncontrolled old-Net entities is real. Digital evidence can be copied, altered, staged, encrypted, or physically destroyed. A netrunner should uncover relationships and systems, not merely pass a skill check that reveals the entire plot. Decide what is online, what is air-gapped, who audits logs, and what happens when a system loses power.

referenceChunks.title: Media, Culture, and Style
referenceChunks.text: Night City is a media environment where reputation, scandal, entertainment, advertising, and political narrative shape reality. Corporate outlets, independent media, pirate broadcasters, microstations, screamsheets, influencers, and rockerboys compete for attention. A story can protect a crew by exposing a client or destroy it by turning footage into spectacle. Style is practical identity. The broader Cyberpunk visual traditions include Entropism, emphasizing survival and necessity; Kitsch, emphasizing bright style over substance; Neomilitarism, emphasizing controlled corporate and military function; and Neokitsch, combining wealth with cultivated display. These labels are most explicit in 2077 material, but the social principle that appearance communicates allegiance and ambition applies in 2045. Music, fashion, clubs, body modification, sports, braindance, street art, and branded products provide belonging in a fractured city. Rockerboys are figures who mobilize emotion and communities through performance and public presence, not only musicians. Media characters require sources, verification, editing, distribution, and protection. Publishing evidence does not guarantee reform; corporations can discredit, bury, buy, or weaponize a story. It can still change what officials and neighborhoods can deny. Give factions visual and cultural language without making every member uniform. A gang's colors, a corporation's architecture, and a nomad family's vehicle markings communicate before dialogue. Let characters intentionally construct their own image and face consequences when others define it for them.

referenceChunks.title: Housing, Services, and Infrastructure
referenceChunks.text: Night City requires electricity, water, sewer, waste collection, transport, banking, education, food distribution, emergency response, and communications. In 2045 these systems are uneven combinations of municipal service, private contracts, corporate infrastructure, neighborhood repair, and improvised alternatives. Housing ranges from corporate residences and renovated apartments to cargo-container units, overcrowded complexes, temporary construction, nomad camps, reclaimed structures, and luxury enclaves. A home provides storage, identity, community, and vulnerability. Rent, service failure, redevelopment, and building security are useful pressures. Medical service includes public emergency response, corporate plans, private hospitals, trauma providers, neighborhood clinics, and unlicensed treatment. Education similarly varies from corporate training and private schools to public systems, apprenticeships, community programs, and self-teaching through the Data Pool. Utilities can be targets and employers. A crew may protect a substation, investigate poisoned water, steal service records, escort repair technicians, or expose a contract designed to force residents out. Infrastructure work creates maps, access credentials, and knowledge that criminals and corporations value. Do not portray every service as permanently failed. The city functions because people maintain it, often under dangerous conditions. Show working systems alongside inequality. A well-lit street may be safe because residents organized maintenance, not because Night City suddenly became benevolent.

referenceChunks.title: Transport, Trade, and Nomads
referenceChunks.text: Night City connects to the wider world by road, rail, sea, and air. Traffic, damaged routes, parking, fuel, checkpoints, vehicle ownership, and public transit shape movement inside the city. A secure vehicle is both transportation and a major asset. Nomad families and nations became essential during the Time of the Red by moving cargo, rebuilding routes, operating heavy equipment, and connecting isolated markets. They are not merely wandering raiders. Family structure, mutual obligation, technical skill, transport access, and reputation support their power. Nomad groups differ in history and method. Some specialize in land convoys, maritime work, construction, salvage, security, entertainment, or migration. The Aldecaldos are famous, but they do not represent every family. The Raffen Shiv are predatory outcasts in common portrayal and should not be used as a label for all hostile nomads without context. Ports and rail yards create chokepoints where city offices, corporations, unions, gangs, fixers, and nomads negotiate. Smuggling can move medicine and refugees as well as weapons and contraband. Travel jobs should include route knowledge, weather, maintenance, cargo priorities, and who owns the road. A convoy ambush is more interesting when the attackers need one container, the client lied about another, and a neighborhood depends on the rest. Nomad characters should have family relationships and responsibilities that matter beyond access to vehicles.

referenceChunks.title: Night City in 2077
referenceChunks.text: By 2077 Night City is a more vertically developed, consumer-saturated, and corporately dominated metropolis than it was in 2045. Arasaka has returned as a central public power, while Militech remains a major rival linked to the New United States. Megabuildings, braindance markets, advanced personal networks, ubiquitous advertising, later cyberware, and familiar video-game districts define this era. The city includes areas such as City Center, Watson, Westbrook, Heywood, Santo Domingo, Pacifica, and the surrounding Badlands. Dogtown is a walled district associated with later political and military developments. Specific gang territories, leaders, corporate facilities, and police conditions differ from 2045. Cyberpunk 2077, Phantom Liberty, and Edgerunners provide canonical stories in this later period, but their protagonists and outcomes should not become mandatory campaign events. A tabletop campaign can use the 2077 status quo before, around, or apart from those stories. Netrunning in 2077 includes capabilities and infrastructure not identical to Cyberpunk RED's local-architecture model. Use the selected ruleset for mechanics rather than translating every video-game effect literally. When a player chooses 2077, load a dedicated era overlay or ask which famous events count. Do not let knowledge of 2077 leak backward into 2045 NPCs. Conversely, do not describe the 2077 city as if it still operates under Red-era scarcity and exclusion of Arasaka.

referenceChunks.title: Common Night City Canon Traps
referenceChunks.text: The primary error is era blending. Night City 2020, the devastated 2023 city, the rebuilding metropolis of 2045, and the corporate megalopolis of 2077 are different operating environments. Attach a year to districts, gangs, corporations, technology, and famous characters. Night City is not a sovereign country. In 2045 it is an independent city within the Free State of Northern California and a free port. It has municipal government even when enforcement is fragmented. Arasaka is not openly dominant in 2045 as it is in 2077. The old global Net is not healthy. Cyberpunk RED netrunning is not universal remote quickhacking. Scarcity and reconstruction still shape the economy. Do not treat cyberware as a costume without medicine or as proof of inevitable murder. Do not reduce nomads to raiders, gangs to random combat encounters, or corporate employees to one class of villain. Famous locations such as the Afterlife can be used when era-appropriate, but the crew should build its own network. Do not make every fixer know every secret or every camera feed available. Night City's brutality is effective because people still build homes, businesses, music, care, and community. If every NPC is treacherous and every system fails, choices lose meaning. When uncertain about a later event, omit it or mark it as campaign-created. A clean 2045 city with fewer named references is more accurate than a glittering mixture of three decades.
